# brig audit prune

Delete audit history

## Synopsis

```text
brig audit prune [VM]
```

## Description

prune deletes audit history, which nothing else does unless audit.retention
in config.yaml is set: the days written before --before, the records of a
sandbox (--sandbox, with -w for another workspace than default), or with
--deleted-vms the whole history of every VM that [`brig delete`](brig-delete.md) deleted.
Without a VM, --before and --deleted-vms work on every VM.

It says what it deletes and how much space that frees. On a terminal it
asks first; --yes skips the question, and --dry-run only says.

## Options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--before string` | delete the days before this date, or before this long ago (90d) |
| `--deleted-vms` | delete the history of VMs that no longer exist |
| `--dry-run` | only say what would be deleted |
| `--sandbox string` | delete the records of this sandbox |
| `-w, --workspace string` | the workspace of the gateway to work in (default: $BRIG\_WORKSPACE, else default) |
| `-y, --yes` | do not ask for confirmation |

The [global options](brig.md#options) of brig apply too.
